views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Enter the May 3–4 Beijing talks ready to exchange views and test whether Washington will pause Section 301 implementation and reopen a ZTE compliance path, without new industrial-policy or purchase commitments. Keep the already-announced $50B mirror list and the implemented $3B Section 232 retaliation in place as leverage; do not add a fresh tariff or non-tariff strike this week. Refuse preconditions on Made in China 2025, and treat any U.S. demand to drop the WTO case as a non-starter until the 301 list itself is frozen.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not yet at the +0.5 high anchor. The April 16 Commerce denial order is a live firm-level shock: ZTE itself said the ban threatens its survival, a U.S. attorney called it a “death sentence,” and Chinese commentary framed it as a wake-up on semiconductor dependence—exactly the “firm-level targeting” the CHN high-threat landmark describes. The April 3 USTR list (~$50B, ~1,300 lines in aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery) is aimed at Made in China 2025, and Trump has already floated a further $100B after China’s April 4 mirror list. That combination raises the ceiling. It is not existential yet: 301 duties are still in a comment period, not in force; Chinese industrial production is still running ~6–7% y/y; CPI is stable; reserves remain ~$3.13T with only a ~1% draw; the yuan is stronger over the 180-day window (6.63 → 6.36), not under FX stress; and merchandise exports have not rolled over. Action should therefore stay at hold/negotiate, not escalate. Further tariffs now would likely harden Lighthizer/Navarro and make it easier for Washington to activate 301 and the $100B threat; unrequited purchase or MIC2025 concessions would cash in China’s leverage before the U.S. has tabled a matching offer. Talks led by Liu He with Mnuchin, Lighthizer, Ross, Navarro and Kudlow are the live venue; a Chinese official has already said Beijing will not negotiate core interests or accept preconditions on MIC2025. The disciplined stance is to talk, keep the existing retaliatory lists, and seek a ZTE/301 pause without writing a check first.
key_factors: ZTE 7-year denial order is a live operational shutdown risk and a revealed semiconductor choke-point
Section 301 $50B list targets MIC2025 sectors but is still proposed, not collected
Trump $100B follow-on threat after China’s April 4 mirror list raises the escalation ceiling
High-level Beijing talks open 3–4 May with a split U.S. delegation; breakthrough viewed as unlikely
China’s real economy is not yet showing trade-war damage: IP ~6–7% y/y, reserves ~$3.13T, yuan firmer over the lookback
Existing $3B (232) and proposed $50B (301) Chinese retaliation already supplies leverage without a new strike

sources_cited.excerpt: US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine, and related items) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
China industrial production still ~106.8 (same period previous year=100) as of 2018-05-01; no trade-war collapse in output.
China reserves excluding gold ~$3.129T as of 2018-05-01, down only ~0.95% over the window.
CNY/USD 6.361 on 2018-05-02 vs 6.631 on 2017-11-06; yuan stronger over the lookback, not under acute FX pressure.
ZTE said the denial order will severely impact its survival; a U.S. attorney described the ban as a death sentence; Commerce official said it is unlikely to lift the ban.

Talks led by Mnuchin and Liu He open Thursday; breakthrough on structural policy viewed as highly unlikely; Chinese official said Beijing will not negotiate core interests or accept preconditions including Made in China 2025.

ZTE ban effectively cripples a firm dependent on Qualcomm chips and Android; economists said China was shocked at how vulnerable Chinese companies are; both sides will seek to avert a trade war but tech is the core disagreement.
After China’s $50B counter-list, Trump asked USTR for additional tariffs on $100B; MOFCOM resolved to fight to the finish; China referred Section 301 to the WTO.
